Future Market Square.name: Future Market Square
Future Market Square.basicInfo:
A flat, cleared rise in the western Westreach staked out with survey cordons and wooden pins — the Chamberlain's first choice for a market square. The ground here is unusually firm and level, roads in imagination already bend toward it from three directions, and the young treants have kept a respectful distance. Cowslip grows thick around the stakes as if decorating the future on the dimension's behalf.

Living Ecology: The measured rise remains alive with cowslip, dawn moths, and a root-safe ring of lantern saplings. Survey cords glow faintly wherever a future foundation can settle without blocking drainage or animal paths.
Future Market Square.hiddenInfo:
The soil here is the most construction-responsive in the Demi-Plane — foundations settle within days instead of weeks. A small well has already surfaced at the square's northeast corner, unmarked and unfinished, apparently the dimension getting a head start. The Chamberlain visits weekly to log ground changes; he has sketched a full market design but refuses to break ground without the creator's word. Objects pinned under the cordon stakes overnight tend to be exactly what the future market's first traders will need.

Ecological Continuity: The site supports the existing Commerce development path but does not summon traders, stock, customers, or buildings. Those require actual access, construction, relationships, and exchange.

Guesthouse Site.name: Guesthouse Site
Guesthouse Site.basicInfo:
A gentle south-facing slope in the central Westreach, staked as the future guesthouse grounds — level ground, good drainage, young trees saved for shade rather than cleared. The first visitors to the dimension will sleep here. A firepit ring has already appeared at the slope's foot, stones laid neatly by no visible hand.

Living Ecology: Foxfire dew beads thickly on the saved shade trees, and dewback tortoises use the slope as a dawn crossing. The spontaneous firepit sits above a natural dry-stone heat seam rather than ordinary copied campcraft.
Guesthouse Site.hiddenInfo:
The dimension pre-built the firepit overnight and the Chamberlain cannot bring himself to move it — it chose the exact spot his own sketches did. Foxfire dew collects here more thickly than anywhere nearby, suggesting the site wants guests welcomed and rested. Harmless sprites have taken up residence in the saved trees, and they rearrange the stakes slightly when they think his spacing is wrong. One territorial spirit beast guards the slope's western edge and must be acknowledged before any construction passes it.

Ecological Continuity: The land anticipates hospitality as usable terrain, not as automatic guests. No visitor learns of or enters the Demi-Plane without established permission and access.

Training Yard Site.name: Training Yard Site
Training Yard Site.basicInfo:
A broad, hard-packed flat in the eastern Westreach closest to the core, staked as the future training yard — the flattest, firmest ground in the region, deliberately kept clear of even sapling trees. The soil compacts underfoot like packed earth of a much older settlement. Face-worn distances make someone standing at one end feel the other end is nearer than it looks: not quite right, but not quite wrong either.

Living Ecology: The compacted ground sheds rain toward a border of shock-absorbing violet moss. Jewel beetles gather harmless residual mana after strenuous movement, keeping repeated practice from scorching the soil.
Training Yard Site.hiddenInfo:
The hard ground is the dimension's doing — the region foresaw combat practice and pre-compacted the soil. Nothing here grows, and footsteps sound of old ground in a young dimension. The slight spatial distortion is probably the mana channel's flow beneath it, making it ideal ground for training perception as well as the body. The Chamberlain keeps this site cleared personally and hopes the creator's oath-sworn residents will one day sweat here.

Ecological Continuity: Its slight spatial compression sharpens distance judgment but does not improve skills, award experience, or force training outcomes on its own. Mechanical advancement remains governed by the established systems.

Dawn Stream.name: Dawn Stream
Dawn Stream.basicInfo:
The young river of The Dawn Barrow — clear water that appeared without instruction, threading the meadow's open ground between wildflower clusters and wet-grass flats. Where it passes over red stone it glows faintly, as if the water and the stone are pleased to meet. The stream feels newly made in the best sense: every bend is a place the dimension noticed and improved, and objects keep arriving in its current from regions far away.

Living Ecology: Ribbonfin flash beneath flower islands, mist swallows skim insects from the bends, and the current changes from silver to violet to gold according to what the upstream regions have recently released.
Dawn Stream.hiddenInfo:
The stream flows out of the Mirror Mere — the dimension's first autonomous connection between its own regions, hydrology designed by no one. It is still growing a personality: some bends pocket a slow warm pool, others sharpen overnight into small waterfalls, and at least one stretch runs over an undercut cave that the water made for hiding. Flower islands — mats of wetland blooms riding slow currents — migrate downstream on windless days. The Chamberlain logs each change with more optimism than any other entry in his ledgers.

Ecological Continuity: The colors record carried material and mana state only. They do not reveal who caused a change, what anyone intended, or unseen events without evidence reaching the water.

Redstone Crossing.name: Redstone Crossing
Redstone Crossing.basicInfo:
The Dawn Stream's only natural ford — a band of red stones across the current that glow faintly beneath clear water, laid like a path the river itself consented to. Meadow deer use it, brook spirits gather beneath it, and the footing is dry and true. From mid-crossing, the whole meadow is visible in its morning colors, flowers turning slowly toward warmth on both banks.

Living Ecology: Redscale lizards bask between dry stepping stones while dawn cranes pick delicately through the shallow downstream fan. Each footfall sends a warm coral pulse through the submerged rock.
Redstone Crossing.hiddenInfo:
The red stones were not placed; the stream surfaced them when it needed a crossing and polished them ever since. Their glow is mana-water reacting to redstone — the same chemistry the Chamberlain hopes to reproduce in future aqueducts. River sprites congregate here to ride the current over the ford, and the stone's underside is dotted with redstone lizards' shed — bright scales worth collecting. One stone, third from the west bank, sounds hollow: something fell between the streambed and the redstone long ago and has not yet surfaced.

Ecological Continuity: The hollow third stone contains a natural root-and-water cavity where redstone accretes around a trapped bubble of concentrated dawnlight. It is a small ecological discovery, not an obligatory quest hook.

Eastern Expansion Site.name: Eastern Expansion Site
Eastern Expansion Site.basicInfo:
The Chamberlain's flagged ground for the Demi-Plane's first eastward development — a broad terrace of hard-packed ground at the Easthold's western edge, staked, measured, and waiting. Mana-stone nodes stud the perimeter, the golden flats approach from three sides, and the air here is always faintly warm without source. This is where anything that needs significant power should be built: the site holds potential under pressure like a coiled spring.

Living Ecology: Gilt scarabs trace cool foundation corridors between warm mana vents, leaving lines of amber dust that the Chamberlain can incorporate into construction plans. Ember shrubs ring the measured terrace without crossing its stakes.
Eastern Expansion Site.hiddenInfo:
The site sits directly above the widest mana channel bleeding off the Mana Heart's circulation — excess energy the dimension cannot yet contain passes beneath it. Foundations here would draw power themselves; a forge built at the site would never lack heat, and a summoning circle would feed itself. The Chamberlain has flagged two mana vents that would serve as natural furnace ports. He has also noticed the hard ground softly humming at dawn — a tone matching a rhythm he does not understand and has privately nicknamed 'the hammer that is coming.'

Ecological Continuity: The site provides a strong, stable power source under the existing development system; it does not complete a forge, workshop, summoning circle, or other project until one is actually chosen and built.

Golden Upland.name: Golden Upland
Golden Upland.basicInfo:
The broad sunlit plain of The Easthold — harder ground, golden dry-grass flats, and the richest light in the dimension, warm without a source. Dust motes hang in the air like slow sparks of gold, unmoving. The upland feels like the space where the dimension is pushing outward against its own edge: stretching, straining, trying to grow beyond what has been thought of so far.

Living Ecology: Vent moths rise from ember shrubs at dusk, sunscale lizards carry heat into their burrows, and distant hawks bend the gold air around their wings. Cold Mirror Mere wind occasionally sends a moving violet stripe across the northern grass.
Golden Upland.hiddenInfo:
The upland's constant warmth draws phenomena: sun hawks nest in thermal columns of raw mana, mana vents breathe heat and light from stone seams, and hidden workshops have appeared where tools were once imagined strongly — half-formed benches, anvil outlines, racks of unidentifiable instruments that dissolve if studied too directly. Temporary summoning phenomena interrupt the flat ground erratically: half-built circles, calls half-heard. Golden lizards eat mana-stone dust and their shed scales concentrate it — a shortcut prospectors have not yet thought of.

Ecological Continuity: Half-formed workshop shapes are harmless expressions of remembered utility and fade unless development gives them material, labor, and purpose. They contain no free finished equipment or unexplained craftspeople.
